definition_en: a violent collision or its sound, or to hit something hard and break
core_image: 两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃碎成一地亮点
scene: 清晨的十字路口，两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃撒了一地。The two cars crashed at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 crash 指「碰撞」（第 1 个义项：车辆猛烈相撞）；句意是两辆车在路口撞上了。

senses.title: Two things hitting hard
senses.definition: a violent collision between vehicles or objects
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或物体之间的猛烈相撞
senses.example: The crash blocked the whole road.
senses.exampleCN: 这场碰撞把整条路都堵住了。
senses.why: Two paths meet and both refuse to bend.
senses.whyCN: 两条路线相遇，两边都不肯让。

senses.title: An aircraft coming down
senses.definition: the falling and breaking of an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 飞行器坠落并损毁
senses.example: The plane crash was a terrible accident.
senses.exampleCN: 那场空难是一场可怕的意外。
senses.why: What flies must also obey the ground.
senses.whyCN: 会飞的东西，也终究要听地面的话。

senses.title: A market falling down
senses.definition: a sudden failure of a market or a system
senses.definitionCN: 市场或系统的突然失效
senses.example: The market crash ruined many families.
senses.exampleCN: 市场崩溃让许多家庭破了产。
senses.why: Numbers can fall as fast as metal can.
senses.whyCN: 数字下坠的速度，不比金属慢。

intro.en: Crash comes from Middle English crasschen, to make a loud clattering noise, a word built from its own sound.
intro.cn: crash 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是照着声音造出来的词。

items.en: Crasschen meant to make a loud clattering noise.
items.cn: crasschen 意为发出响亮的碰撞声。

items.en: Crash named the sound of something breaking.
items.cn: crash 指东西碎裂时的响声。

items.en: It came to name a violent collision itself.
items.cn: 它转而来指猛烈碰撞这件事本身。

items.en: Crash widened to aircraft and to money markets.
items.cn: crash 又扩展到飞机与金融市场。

items.en: It now covers traffic, planes, computers and prices.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖交通、飞机、电脑与价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin with a hard cr-, and the meaning group names other words for violent impact.
note.cn: 形近组收集以硬辅音 cr- 开头的词，近义组列出其他表示猛烈撞击的说法。

entries.definition: to press something until it breaks
a sharp disagreement or fight
a hard outer layer
the hitting together of two moving things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two bumpers meeting, then move to a falling plane and to a falling market.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个保险杠相碰开始，再到坠落的飞机，最后到崩落的市场。

normal.en: Crash sounds like what it means: a hard thing meeting a hard thing.
normal.cn: crash 读起来就像它的意思：硬东西撞上硬东西。

normal.en: Glass tells the story best, because it breaks all at once.
normal.cn: 玻璃最能说明问题，因为它是整片一起碎的。

normal.en: A crash course is a short road driven at full speed.
normal.cn: 速成课就是全速开完的一小段路。

normal.en: A plane crash ends in silence after the noise.
normal.cn: 空难总是在巨响之后归于寂静。

normal.en: Prices crash the way glass does: no warning, then nothing.
normal.cn: 价格崩落像玻璃：没有预告，然后什么都没有。

abstract.en: Picture two metal heads touching at speed.
abstract.cn: 想象两个金属车头高速相触。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart dropping straight down.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线笔直落下。

abstract.en: Picture a shower of small bright pieces on the road.
abstract.cn: 想象路面上撒开一片明亮的小碎片。

examples.en: The truck crashed into the fence.
examples.cn: 卡车撞上了篱笆。

examples.en: He survived a plane crash last winter.
examples.cn: 他去年冬天经历了一场空难并活了下来。

examples.en: The stock market crashed in a single day.
examples.cn: 股市在一天之内崩盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crash 记成「咔嚓」加 sh：撞上去那一声碎响，就是 crash。

root: 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是拟声词，本指物体碎裂的响声，后指猛烈碰撞，近代又扩展到飞机坠毁与市场崩溃。

sensesIntro.en: From two cars meeting to a plane coming down and a market losing its floor.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两车相撞，到飞机坠落，最后到市场失去支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hard fronts meeting with a burst of glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个坚硬的车头相撞，玻璃四溅。

branches.en: Two moving things reach the same point at once.
branches.cn: 两个运动的东西同时到达同一点。

branches.en: What flies can lose the air under it.
branches.cn: 会飞的东西也会失去身下的空气。

branches.en: A system built on numbers can fall like metal.
branches.cn: 建立在数字上的系统也能像金属一样跌落。

branches.en: Both end with broken parts on the ground.
branches.cn: 两者都以碎片落地收场。

branches.en: The same word covers a lost plane and a lost fortune.
branches.cn: 同一个词既说失事的飞机，也说失去的财富。

intro.en: Crash is an imitative base word that builds compounds with course, landing and proof.
intro.cn: crash 是拟声词根，可与 course、landing、proof 等组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English; Latin offers no source for this crash.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，拉丁语并不能给它提供来源。

A crashing sound came from the hall.
A party crasher ate all the cake.

items.meaning: a short fast course of study
items.example: He took a crash course in Spanish.

items.meaning: a landing that damages the aircraft

definition_en: a large bowl-shaped hole in the ground
core_image: 地面凹陷成一只巨大的碗
scene: 山顶有一个巨大的火山口。A huge crater opened at the summit.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crater 指火山口；句意是山顶裂开了一个巨大的火山口。

senses.definition: the bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano

senses.example: Smoke rose from the crater.
senses.exampleCN: 烟从火山口升起。
senses.why: A giant bowl in the mountain.

senses.title: Impact hollow

senses.why: A fist pressed into soft clay.

senses.title: Bowl on the moon
senses.definition: a round hollow on a planet or moon surface
senses.definitionCN: 行星或月球表面的圆形凹地
senses.example: Telescopes show craters on the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜能看到月球上的环形山。
senses.why: Moon craters printed in dust.
senses.whyCN: 尘土里印出的月坑。

definition_en: to want something very strongly
core_image: 喉咙发干，满脑子只想着那一口水
scene: 熬夜之后他特别想吃点甜的。After the long night he craved something sweet.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：crave 指渴望；句意是熬了一夜后他特别想吃甜的。

senses.definition: to want something very much
senses.definitionCN: 非常想要某物

senses.exampleCN: 他特别想喝杯冷饮。
senses.why: A dry throat and one glass of water.
senses.whyCN: 干渴的喉咙和一杯水。

senses.title: Beg for

senses.definitionCN: 低声下气地请求

senses.exampleCN: 她恳求他的原谅。
senses.why: Hands held out for mercy.

senses.title: Body hunger

senses.definitionCN: 脸朝下、速度最快的一种游泳姿势
senses.example: She swam the crawl across the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 她用自由泳游过了泳池。
senses.why: In water the body lies flat and pulls itself forward.
senses.whyCN: 在水里，身体放平，用手把自己往前拉。

intro.en: Crawl comes from Middle English crawlen, probably from an Old Norse word meaning to claw or scratch.
intro.cn: crawl 源自中古英语 crawlen，很可能来自一个意为用爪抓扒的古诺斯语词。

items.en: Krafla meant to claw or scratch with the hands.
items.cn: krafla 意为用手抓或扒。

items.en: Crawlen meant to move low, pulling with the limbs.
items.cn: crawlen 意为贴低身子、用四肢拉着前进。

items.en: Crawl named the slow creeping of a child.
items.cn: crawl 指孩子缓慢地匍匐前行。

items.en: It widened to slow traffic and to a swimming stroke.
items.cn: 它扩展到缓慢的车流和一种泳姿。

items.en: It now covers babies, queues and the front crawl.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖婴儿、排队的队伍与自由泳。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that rhyme with crawl, and the meaning group names other ways of slow movement.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 crawl 押韵的词，近义组列出其他缓慢移动的说法。

entries.definition: a noisy fight among several people
to speak slowly with long vowels
to write in a quick untidy way
to move slowly and quietly
to go up using hands and feet
to move forward a tiny bit at a time

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a baby on the floor, then move to a queue in a tunnel and to a swimmer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从地上的婴儿开始，再到隧道里的车流，最后到游泳的人。

normal.en: Crawl begins with a scratching sound: hands pulling at the ground.
normal.cn: crawl 开头带着抓扒的意味：手在地面上拉。

normal.en: A baby crawls before it walks, because the floor is closer.
normal.cn: 婴儿先爬后走，因为地面更近。

normal.en: Traffic that crawls is a long metal animal with no legs.
normal.cn: 缓慢的车流，是一头没有腿的长金属动物。

normal.en: In the front crawl your arms behave like small oars.
normal.cn: 游自由泳时，两条手臂就像两支小桨。

normal.en: Anything moving an inch a minute is crawling.
normal.cn: 任何一分钟只挪一点点的东西，都在 crawl。

abstract.en: Picture small palms pressed flat on a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 想象小小的手掌平按在木地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a line of red lights moving one metre at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一串红色尾灯一次只挪一米。

abstract.en: Picture a face turning sideways for a quick breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸侧过去快速换气。

examples.en: The child crawled under the table.
examples.cn: 孩子爬到桌子底下。

examples.en: Cars crawled along the flooded road.
examples.cn: 汽车在积水的路上缓慢行驶。

examples.en: He can swim the crawl for an hour.
examples.cn: 他能用自由泳游一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crawl 记成 cr（抓）加 awl（锥子）：像锥子一样贴着地面，一边抓一边往前。

root: 源自中古英语 crawlen，可能来自古诺斯语 krafla（用爪抓扒），本指贴地用手脚扒着前进，后引申为缓慢移动与一种游泳姿势。

sensesIntro.en: From a body low on the floor to a queue in slow motion and a swimmer pulling water.
sensesIntro.cn: 从贴在地面的身体，到慢动作的车流，最后到划水的泳者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body close to the ground, pulling itself forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具贴近地面的小身体把自己往前拉。

branches.en: Hands and knees take turns carrying the body.
branches.cn: 手和膝轮流把身体带向前。

branches.en: A long line of cars moves at the speed of a crawl.
branches.cn: 一长串车以爬行的速度前进。

branches.en: In water the same low posture becomes speed.
branches.cn: 在水里，同样的低姿态变成了速度。

branches.en: Slow and low is the shared picture of both.
branches.cn: 又低又慢，是两者共有的画面。

branches.en: One crawl is slow on land and fast in water.
branches.cn: 同一个词，在陆上慢，在水里快。

intro.en: Crawl is a native base word that builds the agent -er, the adjective -y and compounds with space.
intro.cn: crawl 是本族词根，可加 -er 表人、-y 表性质，并与 space 等构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, with no Latin base behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，背后没有拉丁词基。

items.example: He does ten crawls across the pool.
items.exampleCN: 他在泳池里游十个来回。

items.example: The ant crawled up my arm.

items.meaning: a creature or machine that crawls
items.example: A crawler moved along the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 一台履带机器沿管道移动。
那间黑地窖让人心里发毛。

items.meaning: a low space under a house
items.exampleCN: 管道从房屋底下的低层穿过。

items.example: He teaches the front crawl first.

definition_en: mad or unable to think normally, extremely fond of something, or very foolish
core_image: 一个人把椅子顶在头上，在雨里转圈大笑
scene: 他把椅子顶在头上，在雨里转着圈大笑。The neighbours thought he was crazy.
sceneCN: 这里 crazy 指「疯狂的」（第 1 个义项：精神或行为失去常态）；句意是邻居们都觉得他疯了。

senses.title: A mind out of order
senses.definition: mad, or unable to think or behave in a normal way
senses.definitionCN: 精神失常，或无法正常思考和行事
senses.example: The noise nearly drove him crazy.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声几乎把他逼疯。
senses.why: When the mind loses its order, the body does strange things.
senses.whyCN: 脑子一乱，身体就做出古怪的举动。

senses.title: Wildly fond of something
senses.definition: extremely fond of something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某物或某人喜欢到极点
senses.example: She is crazy about old films.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老电影着迷得不得了。
senses.why: Love also takes away the usual measure.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢到极点，也会拿走平常的分寸。

senses.title: A plan without sense
senses.definition: very foolish or unreasonable
senses.definitionCN: 极为愚蠢或不合理的
senses.example: It is a crazy plan that cannot work.
senses.exampleCN: 这是个不可能成功的荒唐计划。
senses.why: A plan without measure looks like a mind without order.
senses.whyCN: 没有分寸的计划，就像没有秩序的脑子。

intro.en: Crazy grows from Middle English crasen, to shatter, so it first meant full of cracks and unsound.
intro.cn: crazy 由中古英语 crasen（碎裂）而来，所以最初意为「满是裂缝、不结实」。

items.en: Crasen meant to break or shatter.
items.cn: crasen 意为打碎或裂开。

items.en: Crazy first meant full of cracks and unsound.
items.cn: crazy 最初指布满裂缝、不牢靠。

items.en: It came to mean a mind that is cracked.
items.cn: 它转而指「裂了缝的脑子」。

items.en: It widened to mean wildly fond of something.
items.cn: 它又扩展为对某物喜欢到发狂。

items.en: It now covers madness, passion and foolish plans.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖发疯、痴迷与荒唐的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near crazy in shape, and the meaning group names other words for foolish or wild.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 crazy 的词，近义组列出其他表示疯狂与愚蠢的说法。

entries.definition: a fashion that everyone follows for a while
driven mad by strong feeling
entries.definitionCN: 被强烈情绪逼得失常的

entries.definition: a line pressed into cloth or paper
entries.definitionCN: 布料或纸上压出的折痕

entries.definition: mentally ill or wildly foolish
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常或荒唐至极的

entries.definition: lacking good sense
out of control and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 失去控制且充满蛮劲的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with cracks in a pot, then move to a cracked mind and to a passion with no measure.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从罐子上的裂缝开始，再到裂了缝的脑子，最后到没有分寸的痴迷。

normal.en: Crazy comes from a word for cracked, and a cracked pot cannot hold water.
normal.cn: crazy 来自「裂」这个词，裂了的罐子存不住水。

normal.en: A cracked mind lets strange ideas leak out.
normal.cn: 脑子裂了缝，古怪的念头就漏出来。

normal.en: Being crazy about a film is a happy crack in the heart.
normal.cn: 对一部电影着迷，是心里一条快乐的裂缝。

normal.en: A crazy plan is a bridge with no supports.
normal.cn: 荒唐的计划，是一座没有支柱的桥。

normal.en: Noise repeated all day can crack anyone's calm.
normal.cn: 噪声一整天不停，能敲裂任何人的平静。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline crack running down a clay pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一道发丝般的裂缝从陶罐上延伸下来。

abstract.en: Picture a man laughing in the rain with a chair on his head.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头顶椅子在雨里大笑的人。

abstract.en: Picture a map with the roads drawn in the wrong places.
abstract.cn: 想象一张把路画错位置的地图。

examples.en: He is crazy about fast cars.
examples.cn: 他对快车着迷。

examples.en: It was a crazy idea, but it worked.
examples.cn: 那是个疯狂的想法，但它奏效了。

examples.en: The children drove their mother crazy with noise.
examples.cn: 孩子们吵得妈妈要发疯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crazy 记成 crack（裂）加 y：脑子裂了缝，人就成了 crazy。

root: 源自中古英语 crasen（碎裂）；crazy 本指「满是裂缝、不结实的」，后指「脑子出了裂缝」即发疯，再引申为极度着迷与荒唐。

sensesIntro.en: From a cracked thing, to a mind that loses order, to a fondness that has no limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从裂了的东西，到失去秩序的脑子，最后到没有限度的喜欢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack opening in something that should be whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该完整的东西上裂开一道缝。

branches.en: A mind with a crack no longer follows one line.
branches.cn: 裂了缝的脑子不再沿着一条线走。

branches.en: Passion also breaks the usual limits of attention.
branches.cn: 痴迷同样打破了注意力的常规限度。

branches.en: A plan with no support looks like a cracked wall.
branches.cn: 没有支撑的计划，像一堵裂开的墙。

branches.en: Both are states where measure has been lost.
branches.cn: 两者都是失去分寸的状态。

branches.en: Love and folly both ignore what others call sense.
branches.cn: 痴迷与荒唐，都不理别人所谓的分寸。

intro.en: Crazy begins with the base craze and takes the endings -y, -ily and -iness.
intro.cn: crazy 以词基 craze 为底，加上 -y、-ily 与 -iness 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; Latin has no share in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语，拉丁语与它无关。

items.meaningCN: 满是裂缝的，继而指发疯
items.exampleCN: 这个计划听起来很疯狂。

items.example: Each idea was crazier than the last.
items.exampleCN: 每个主意都比上一个更荒唐。

items.example: That was the craziest week of my life.
items.exampleCN: 那是我一生中最疯狂的一周。

items.example: He drove crazily down the hill.

items.exampleCN: 到早晨，那股疯狂劲就过去了。
这种玩具成了一阵风潮。

items.example: A crazed look crossed his face.

items.meaningCN: 被关久了而烦躁不安的
items.example: The crew grew stir-crazy below deck.
items.exampleCN: 船员在甲板下憋得烦躁起来。

definition_en: to make something new that did not exist before
core_image: 一张白纸上第一次画出一扇门，推开就是新房间
scene: 白纸上本来什么都没有，她一笔画出第一扇门。The writer created a whole world in three pages.
sceneCN: 这里 create 指「创造」（第 1 个义项：从无到有地做出新东西）；句意是作者用三页纸创造了一整个世界。

senses.title: To make something new
senses.definition: to make something new that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 做出以前不存在的全新事物
senses.example: They created a garden on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋顶上造了一个花园。
senses.why: A blank space waits for the first line.
senses.whyCN: 一片空白总在等第一笔。

senses.title: To make a work of art
senses.definition: to produce a work of art or writing
senses.definitionCN: 产出艺术作品或文字作品
senses.example: She created a character we all remember.
senses.exampleCN: 她创作了一个我们都记得的角色。
senses.why: A story begins as nothing and then has a face.
senses.whyCN: 故事从无开始，然后长出一张脸。

senses.title: To cause a situation
senses.definition: to cause a situation or a problem to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况或问题发生
senses.example: The new road created a lot of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的路带来了很多噪声。
senses.why: Every new thing pushes the old arrangement aside.
senses.whyCN: 每件新东西都会把旧的安排挤到一边。

intro.en: Create comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, a word related to crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: create 源自拉丁语 creare（制造、使生成），与 crescere（生长）同源。

items.en: Creare meant to make, bring forth or appoint.
items.cn: creare 意为制造、使产生或任命。

items.en: Crescere, to grow, shared the same old root.
items.cn: 表示生长的 crescere 与它共用一个古老词根。

items.en: Creatio named the act of making.
items.cn: creatio 指制造这一行为。

items.en: Create entered English as a word for divine making.
items.cn: create 进入英语时，多指神明造物。

items.en: It now covers art, jobs, problems and accounts.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖艺术创作、就业、问题与账户。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near create in shape, and the meaning group names other words for bringing something into being.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 create 的词，近义组列出其他表示「使某物出现」的说法。

entries.definition: a living animal or being
to burn a body to ashes
a large box for carrying goods
to form something from parts
to think of and build something new
to bring something into existence

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with an empty page, then move to a story and to a change nobody asked for.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张空页开始，再到一个故事，最后到一场没人要求的变化。

normal.en: Create and grow share a root: to create is to let something grow out of nothing.
normal.cn: create 与「生长」同根：创造就是让东西从无里长出来。

normal.en: The first line on a blank page is always the bravest.
normal.cn: 白纸上的第一笔，总是最勇敢的一笔。

normal.en: A writer creates people who never breathe but stay alive.
normal.cn: 作家创造的人从不呼吸，却一直活着。

normal.en: A new road creates noise as well as shortcuts.
normal.cn: 新路带来捷径，也带来噪声。

normal.en: To create an account is to open a small new room.
normal.cn: 创建一个账户，就是开出一间小小的新房间。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil touching white paper for the first time.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔第一次碰到白纸。

abstract.en: Picture a door drawn on a wall, opening inward.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上画着一扇朝里开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a small seed pushing soil upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒小种子把泥土顶起来。

examples.en: The company plans to create two hundred jobs.
examples.cn: 这家公司计划创造两百个就业岗位。

examples.en: He created the whole design on a single sheet.
examples.cn: 他在一张纸上完成了整个设计。

examples.en: Loud music can create tension between neighbours.
examples.cn: 大声的音乐会在邻里之间造成紧张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 create 记成 cre（生长）加 ate：让原本没有的东西长出来，就是创造。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（制造、使生成、任命），与 crescere（生长）同源，本指使某物生成，后指从无到有地造出，也指引起某种状况。

sensesIntro.en: From a blank page to a made world and to the changes that follow it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张白纸，到被造出的世界，最后到随之而来的种种变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first line appearing on empty paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：空白的纸上出现第一笔。

branches.en: Something new is drawn where nothing stood.
branches.cn: 在原本空无的地方画出了新东西。

branches.en: A made character can outlive the hand that drew it.
branches.cn: 被创作的角色能比画它的手活得更久。

branches.en: Every new thing also makes old things move.
branches.cn: 每件新东西也会叫旧东西让位。

branches.en: To create a thing and to create a story share one gesture.
branches.cn: 造物与创作，共用同一个动作。

branches.en: Works and problems both begin with someone acting.
branches.cn: 作品与麻烦，都始于有人动手。

intro.en: Create grows from the Latin making base cre-, with forms in -es, -ed, -ing and nouns in -ion and -or.
intro.cn: create 从拉丁语表示制造的词基 cre- 长出，带 -es、-ed、-ing 等变形，及 -ion、-or 等名词。

latinIntro.en: The making base creare also shapes creation, creator and creature.
latinIntro.cn: 表示制造的词基 creare 也构成 creation、creator 与 creature。

items.meaning: to bring something new into being

items.exampleCN: 这座公园建于一九零零年。

items.example: She is creating a new pattern.
items.exampleCN: 她正在创造一种新花样。

items.meaning: the act or result of making
the power to make new things

definition_zh: 创造；创建；创作；创作物；产物
definition_en: the act of making something exist that did not exist before, or the thing that is made
core_image: 空白的画布上落下第一笔，一件原本不存在的东西出现了
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，人们围在一幅巨大的新画前低声赞叹，作者站在角落。Everyone admired the young artist's latest creation.
sceneCN: 这里 creation 指「创作物」（第 3 个义项：被创作出来的具体作品）；句意是所有人都赞叹这位年轻画家最新的作品。

senses.title: The act of making something new
senses.definition: the act or process of making something exist that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不存在的东西得以存在的行为或过程
senses.example: The creation of new jobs helped the town recover.
senses.exampleCN: 新岗位的创造帮助这个镇子恢复了元气。
senses.why: The Latin stem creare means to bring forth, so the noun first names the act of bringing forth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 creare 意为「使生出」，所以名词首先指「使生出」这一行为本身。

senses.title: The act of inventing or designing
senses.definition: the act of producing a work of art, writing, or design using imagination
senses.definitionCN: 凭想象力产出艺术、文字或设计作品的行为
senses.example: The creation of the character took the author ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个人物的创作花了作者十年时间。
senses.why: When what is brought forth is imagined rather than manufactured, the word narrows to artistic making.
senses.whyCN: 当「生出」的东西来自想象而非制造时，这个词收窄为艺术创作。

senses.title: A thing that has been made
senses.definition: something that someone has made or invented, especially something unusual or imaginative
senses.definitionCN: 某人造出或发明的东西，尤指独特或富有想象力之物
senses.example: The garden is his most unusual creation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是他最不寻常的创作。
senses.why: A finished act of making leaves behind an object, so the noun also names the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 完成的创造会留下一个对象，于是名词也转指这个被造出来的东西。

senses.title: The making of the world
senses.definition: the making of the world and everything in it, especially in religious belief
senses.definitionCN: 世界及其中万物的被造，尤见于宗教信仰
senses.example: The story describes the creation of the world in seven days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲述了世界在七日内被造的过程。
senses.why: Only a supreme maker can bring the whole world forth, so the word rises to the cosmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 能把整个世界生出来的唯有至高造物者，于是这个词升格到宇宙尺度。

senses.title: The whole world of living things
senses.definition: all the living things in the world, thought of together
senses.definitionCN: 把世上一切生灵合起来看的整体
senses.example: All creation seemed to fall silent before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，天地众生仿佛都安静了下来。
senses.why: Every living thing is a made thing, so the made world as a whole can be called creation.
senses.whyCN: 每个生灵都是被造之物，于是被造的世界整体也可以称为「万物」。

intro.en: Creation comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatio, the act of making.
intro.cn: creation 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatio（创造行为）进入英语。

items.en: The root *ker- is generally reconstructed as meaning to grow or make grow.
items.cn: 词根 *ker- 一般被重构为「生长、使生长」之义。

items.en: Creare meant to make something come forth or grow; creatio named the act of making.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生出或生长；creatio 指创造这一行为。

items.en: Creacion carried the same religious and general sense of making.
items.cn: creacion 带有同样泛指与宗教意义上的「创造」义。

items.en: Creation first appeared in English chiefly for the making of the world by God.
items.cn: creation 初入英语时主要指上天创造世界。

items.en: It widened to any act of making and to the thing made, including works of art.
items.cn: 它扩展为任何创造行为及其产物，包括艺术作品。

items.en: It now covers founding things, inventing designs, and naming the results.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖创建事物、设计发明，并指创造出来的成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the near-meaning group names other acts or results of making.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 词干，近义组列出其他表示创造行为或成果的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new exist
good at making new and original things
entries.definitionCN: 善于造出新颖原创之物的

entries.definition: a person or force that makes something
a new device or idea that someone has thought up
entries.definitionCN: 想出来的新装置或新点子

entries.definition: a piece of art, music, or writing
entries.definitionCN: 一件艺术、音乐或文字作品

entries.definition: a work of art made with great skill
entries.definitionCN: 以高超技艺完成的艺术作品

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the first stroke on a blank canvas to the finished thing hanging on the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从空白画布上的第一笔，一直走到挂在墙上的成品。

normal.en: Create plus -ion: the act of creating, then the thing created.
normal.cn: create 加 -ion：先指创造这一行为，再指被造出来的东西。

normal.en: Creation = creation of jobs, creation of art, creation of the world.
normal.cn: creation 的三大常用面：创造岗位、艺术创作、创世。

normal.en: Every creation needs a creator.
normal.cn: 每件创作物背后都有一个创造者。

normal.en: The -ion ending turns the verb into a noun you can count.
normal.cn: -ion 后缀把动词变成可数的名词。

normal.en: Creation and creative share the same first letters and the same family.
normal.cn: creation 与 creative 同头同族，一起记。

abstract.en: Picture the first brushstroke on a blank canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象空白画布上落下的第一笔。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay slowly becoming a figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土慢慢变成一个人像。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn star lighting an empty sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗新星照亮空无一物的天空。

examples.en: The creation of the park took only two years.
examples.cn: 这座公园的建成只花了两年。

examples.en: Her latest creation won first prize at the fair.
examples.cn: 她的最新作品在展会上得了头奖。

examples.en: They discussed stories about the creation of the world.
examples.cn: 他们讨论了关于创世的种种故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creation 记成 create（创造）加 -ion：创造这一行为是创造，创造出来的东西也是创作，一横一竖正好两个方向。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），名词形式 creatio 指「创造行为」，经古法语 creacion 于十四世纪进入英语；本义是「使某物生出」，先专指上天创世，后扩展到一切创造行为及其产物。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare act of making something exist, creation widens to artistic invention, then to the thing made, and finally to the making of the world itself.
sensesIntro.cn: creation 从「使某物存在」的赤裸行为出发，扩展到艺术创作，再转指创作物，最终上升到创世与天地众生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stroke on a blank canvas — something now exists that did not exist before
core.cn: 核心意象：空白画布上的第一笔——原本不存在的东西从此存在了

branches.en: Bringing jobs, systems, or organizations into existence.
branches.cn: 使岗位、体系或组织从无到有。

branches.en: Imagining and designing a work of art or writing.
branches.cn: 凭想象设计与产出艺术或文字作品。

branches.en: The finished object that the act of making leaves behind.
branches.cn: 创造行为留下的成品本身。

branches.en: The religious account of the world being made.
branches.cn: 宗教中世界被造的叙事。

branches.en: All living things viewed as one made world.
branches.cn: 把一切生灵看作同一个被造的世界。

intro.en: Creation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix; the same family shares one stem.
intro.cn: creation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成；同族词共享同一个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Latin creare, and the suffix -ion goes back to Latin -io, which turns verbs into nouns of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到拉丁语 creare，后缀 -ion 源自拉丁语 -io，用于把动词变成表行为的名词。

items.example: create means to make something new
items.exampleCN: create 意为造出新的东西

items.example: action means the act of doing
items.exampleCN: action 意为做这件事的行为

items.example: creativity means the quality of being creative

definition_zh: 有创造力的；创作性的；创意人员
definition_en: good at making new things or ideas, or relating to such making
core_image: 桌上散着纸片和线头，中间立着一个刚拧成的小装置
scene: 桌上散着纸片和线头，他随手把它们拧成一个奇怪的小装置。She found a creative solution to the noise problem.
sceneCN: 这里 creative 指「有创造力的」（第 1 个义项：善于想出并做出新东西）；句意是她为噪声问题想出了一个有创意的办法。

senses.title: Full of new ideas
senses.definition: able to think of new and original ideas
senses.definitionCN: 能想出新颖独到的点子
senses.example: She is the most creative person in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她是班上最有创造力的人。
senses.why: The mind refuses the first easy answer.
senses.whyCN: 这样的脑子不肯接受第一个省事的答案。

senses.title: Involving imagination
senses.definition: involving imagination in making something
senses.definitionCN: 在制作过程中需要想象力的
senses.example: He teaches creative writing at school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校教创意写作。
senses.why: Some work begins with a blank page, not a rule.
senses.whyCN: 有些工作从一张白纸开始，而不是从一条规则开始。

senses.title: A person paid for ideas
senses.definition: a person whose job is to produce ideas
senses.definitionCN: 以想出点子为职业的人
senses.example: The agency hired two creatives.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘了两名创意人员。
senses.why: Every industry needs someone to imagine first.
senses.whyCN: 每个行业都需要有人先想一步。

intro.en: Creative joins Latin creare, to make, with the adjective ending -ive.
intro.cn: creative 由拉丁语 creare（制造）与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

items.en: Creare meant to make or bring forth.
items.cn: creare 意为制造或使产生。

items.en: Creativus named the power to make.
items.cn: creativus 指制造的能力。

items.en: Creative described the power of a maker.
items.cn: creative 形容创造者的能力。

items.en: It widened to art and to original thought.
items.cn: 它扩展到艺术与独到的想法。

items.en: It now also names people paid for their ideas.
items.cn: 今天它也可以指靠点子吃饭的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the create base or a similar ending, and the meaning group names other words for original thinking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 create 词基或相近词尾，近义组列出其他表示原创想法的说法。

entries.definition: a person who makes something new
the act or result of making
acting only after something happens
entries.definitionCN: 只在事情发生后才作出反应的

entries.definition: new and not copied from others
full of pictures in the mind
good at thinking up new things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pile of odd pieces, then move to a blank page and to a paid idea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一堆零碎东西开始，再到一张白纸，最后到一份能卖钱的点。

normal.en: Creative is create with -ive: the quality of being able to make.
normal.cn: creative 就是 create 加 -ive：能造出东西的那种性质。

normal.en: A creative person keeps the odd pieces others throw away.
normal.cn: 有创造力的人会留下别人扔掉的零碎。

normal.en: Two sticks and a string can become a small machine.
normal.cn: 两根棍一段线，也能变成一台小机器。

normal.en: Creative writing starts where the rule book stops.
normal.cn: 创意写作从规则手册结束的地方开始。

normal.en: An agency pays creatives for the ideas it cannot order.
normal.cn: 公司花钱请创意人员，因为他们买不来被命令出的点子。

abstract.en: Picture a table covered with paper, wire and tape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆满纸片、铁丝和胶带的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing that follows no straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅没有一条直线的画。

abstract.en: Picture a light bulb drawn where a full stop should be.
abstract.cn: 想象本该是句号的地方画了一只灯泡。

examples.en: She is creative with very little money.
examples.cn: 她用很少的钱也能做出新花样。

examples.en: The school runs a creative writing club.
examples.cn: 学校办了一个创意写作社。

examples.en: The firm hires young creatives every spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司每年春天都招年轻创意人员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creative 记成 create（创造）加 ive（有…性质的）：有创造性质的，就是有创造力。

root: 由拉丁语 creare（制造、生成）加形容词词尾 -ive 构成；creare 与 crescere（生长）同源，本指「具有生成能力的」，后专指富有创造力与原创想法。

sensesIntro.en: From a mind that refuses the easy answer, to work that begins with a blank page, to people paid for ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不肯接受省事答案的脑子，到从白纸开始的工作，最后到靠点子吃饭的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: odd pieces joined into a shape nobody planned.
core.cn: 核心意象：零碎的东西被拼成没人计划过的形状。

branches.en: The mind keeps looking after the first answer fails.
branches.cn: 第一个答案不行之后，脑子还在继续找。

branches.en: Some work asks for imagination instead of rules.
branches.cn: 有些工作要求想象，而不是规则。

branches.en: An industry pays for the first picture in someone's head.
branches.cn: 行业愿意为某人脑中的第一幅图付钱。

branches.en: The person and the work share one quality of making.
branches.cn: 人与作品共享同一种「造」的品质。

branches.en: A creative job turns ideas into things others can use.
branches.cn: 创意工作把点子变成别人能用的东西。

intro.en: Creative is create plus the adjective ending -ive, and it grows its own nouns and adverbs.
intro.cn: creative 是 create 加形容词词尾 -ive，自身又能长出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin making base creare lies under creative, creation and creator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示制造的词基 creare 垫在 creative、creation 与 creator 之下。

items.example: He created the logo last year.
items.exampleCN: 他去年设计了这个标志。

items.example: They are creating a new app.
items.exampleCN: 他们正在做一个新应用。

items.meaning: the act or result of making
the power to make new things

definition_zh: 创造力；创造性；独创性；创作能力
definition_en: the ability to produce original ideas, works or solutions
core_image: 三样毫不相干的物件在孩子手里被拼成一个能站住的新东西。
scene: 工作室的墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后留下来的方案把两种旧工具合成了一种新用法。The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
sceneCN: 这里 creativity 指「产生原创想法或作品的能力」（第 1 个义项：造出此前不存在之物的总体能力）；句意为墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。可辨识物件：草稿墙、旧工具、工作台、最终方案。

senses.title: The power to make something new
senses.titleCN: 造出新事物的总体能力
senses.definition: the general ability to produce ideas, works or solutions that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 产生此前不存在的观念、作品或解决办法的总体能力
senses.example: The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。
senses.why: The noun is built on create, so it names the power behind making something that was not there.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在「创造」之上，因此指造出原本不存在之物的能力。

senses.title: The quality of being creative
senses.definition: the degree to which an idea or work shows original invention
senses.definitionCN: 一个观念或作品显示原创发明的程度
senses.example: Judges scored the entries for creativity rather than polish.
senses.exampleCN: 评委按创造性而非完成度给参赛作品打分。
senses.why: The abstract noun can name a measurable quality, which is how competitions and schools use it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词可以指一种可测量的性质，比赛与学校正是这样使用它。

senses.title: Originality that stands apart
senses.definition: the quality of being unlike what already exists, especially in a striking way
senses.definitionCN: 与既有之物不同、尤指以显著方式不同的性质
senses.example: The building's creativity lies in what it leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的独创性在于它省略了什么。
senses.why: Newness alone is not enough; the word often implies a difference that others can recognize.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的新还不够；这个词常暗示一种别人能认出的差异。

senses.title: The artist's working power
senses.definition: the capacity to invent and shape works in a medium such as paint, sound or words
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、声音或文字等媒介中发明并塑造作品的能力
senses.example: Her creativity shows most clearly in small drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 她的创作能力在小幅画作中最清楚。
senses.why: Art gives the power a medium, so creativity becomes the ability to shape material into a new form.
senses.whyCN: 艺术给这种能力一个媒介，于是创造力成为把材料塑成新形式的本领。

senses.title: Creativity shared by a group
senses.definition: the combined ability of a group to generate and develop new ideas
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体产生并发展新观念的综合能力
senses.example: Team creativity improved when the quiet members spoke first.
senses.exampleCN: 当沉默的成员先发言时，团队创造力提高了。
senses.why: Organizations treat creativity as a group resource, so the noun is used for a collective rather than one mind.
senses.whyCN: 组织把创造力当作群体资源，因此这个名词用于集体，而非单个头脑。

senses.title: Creative thinking as a process
senses.titleCN: 作为过程的创造性思维
senses.definition: the process of generating, combining and testing novel ideas
senses.definitionCN: 产生、组合并检验新颖观念的过程
senses.example: Creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
senses.exampleCN: 创造力常常是一个制作与丢弃的循环。
senses.why: The noun can name the activity itself, including its failures, not only the final ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指活动本身，包括其中的失败，而不只是最终能力。

senses.title: A period or burst of invention
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which a person or group produces an unusual amount of new work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体产出异常多新作品的一段时间
senses.example: The letters record a burst of creativity before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件记录了战前一次创造力的迸发。
senses.why: Creativity is uneven, so the word also names its high periods rather than a steady trait.
senses.whyCN: 创造力并不均匀，因此这个词也指它的高峰期，而非稳定特质。

senses.title: Inventiveness in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域中的创造能力
senses.definition: the ability to make original contributions within a particular discipline, such as science or business
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定学科、如科学或商业中作出原创贡献的能力
senses.example: Scientific creativity often looks like a better question, not a louder answer.
senses.exampleCN: 科学创造力常常表现为更好的问题，而不是更响亮的答案。
senses.why: Each field defines what counts as new, so the word takes on the standards of that discipline.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都定义什么才算新，因此这个词会带上该学科的标准。

intro.en: Creativity is an English noun formed from creative, which comes from create, from Latin creare, to make or bring forth.
intro.cn: creativity 是由 creative 构成的英语名词；creative 来自 create，而 create 来自拉丁 creare「制造、产生」。

items.en: Creare meant to make, bring forth or produce, and was used of gods, parents and makers alike. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: creare 意为制造、产生或产出，可用于神、父母与制作者。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: The action noun creatio named the making, and in Christian writing it became the word for the creation of the world.
items.cn: 动作名词 creatio 指制造行为；在基督教写作中，它成为「创世」一词。

items.en: English create entered in the fifteenth century through French, first in the sense of bringing something into existence.
items.cn: 英语 create 在十五世纪经法语进入，最初指使某物存在。

items.en: Creative added the adjective suffix to create in the seventeenth century; for a long time it described a divine or artistic making.
items.cn: creative 在十七世纪由 create 加形容词后缀而成；很长时间里它描述神圣或艺术的创造。

items.en: Creativity appeared as a noun in the nineteenth century, and psychology made it a measurable subject in the twentieth.
items.cn: creativity 在十九世纪作为名词出现，心理学在二十世纪把它变成可测量的研究对象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first recorded use of creativity and pre-Latin origin of make): the earliest English citation of the noun is not firmly dated, and the deeper source of creare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词首次记录与「制造」义的拉丁语之前来源）：creativity 最早的英语书证没有确切年代；creare 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the making family that are easy to confuse; group two holds near names for inventive power.
note.cn: 第一组是「制造」词族中容易混淆的词；第二组是表示创造能力的近义词。

entries.definition: The act of making something, or the thing made; creativity is the ability behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的动作，或被造之物；creativity 是背后的能力。

entries.definition: A person who makes something; the maker is not the power that the maker uses.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的人；制造者并不等于他所运用的能力。

entries.definition: Having the power to create; creativity is the noun for that power.
entries.definitionCN: 具有创造能力的；creativity 是这种能力的名词。

entries.definition: The producing of offspring, from a prefix meaning for or forward plus creare; it is not the same as artistic creativity.
entries.definitionCN: 生育后代，由表示「为了、向前」的前缀加 creare 构成；与艺术创造力不同。

entries.definition: The power to picture what is absent or unreal; creativity puts such pictures into works.
entries.definitionCN: 想象不在场或不真实之物的能力；创造力把这类画面变成作品。

entries.definition: A new method or product, especially one that is put into use; innovation stresses adoption, creativity the making.
entries.definitionCN: 新的方法或产品，尤其指被投入使用的；innovation 强调采用，creativity 强调制造。

entries.definition: The quality of being unlike others; originality is one face of creativity, but creativity also covers usefulness and process.
entries.definitionCN: 与众不同的性质；独创性是创造力的一个面向，但创造力也涵盖实用性与过程。

entries.definition: Something new that has been devised; invention is the product, creativity the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 被设计出的新东西；发明是产物，创造力是能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the make root, the noun chain from create to creativity, and the wall of rejected drafts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「制造」词根、从 create 到 creativity 的名词链，以及贴满被否草稿的墙。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to make or bring forth; the noun chain runs create, creative, creativity.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为制造或产生；名词链依次是 create、creative、creativity。

normal.en: The family runs create, creation, creative, creator, creativity and creatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 create、creation、creative、creator、creativity 与 creatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: artistic creativity, team creativity, creativity research.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术创造力、团队创造力、创造力研究。

normal.en: The word names a capacity, a quality and a period: a person has it, a work shows it, a year can be one.
normal.cn: 这个词兼指能力、性质与时期：人有它，作品显示它，某一年也可以是它。

normal.en: Rejected drafts are part of the word: creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
normal.cn: 被否掉的草稿也是这个词的一部分：创造力常常是制作与丢弃的循环。

abstract.en: Picture three unrelated objects lying together until a child joins them into something that stands.
abstract.cn: 想象三件毫不相干的物件躺在一起，直到孩子把它们拼成一个能站住的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of crossed-out drawings with one clean sheet at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一面画满又被划掉的墙，尽头只剩一张干净的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that becomes a tree no one had planted before.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子长成一棵从前无人种过的树。

examples.en: The workshop was designed to give employees time for creativity.
examples.cn: 这个工作坊的设计是为了给员工留出发挥创造力的时间。

examples.en: Creativity rarely appears on a schedule, but it can be given room.
examples.cn: 创造力很少按日程出现，但可以给它空间。

examples.en: Her creativity turned a broken bicycle into a garden cart.
examples.cn: 她的创造力把一辆坏自行车改成了园艺推车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把没有关系的东西拼成一个站得住的新东西 → 创造力

root: 拉丁 creare「制造、产生」→ 动作名词 creatio → 英语 create；加形容词后缀成 creative，再加抽象名词后缀成 creativity。creare 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: something new is brought into being, and the same power is read as a quality, an originality, an artistic skill, a group resource, a process, a burst and a field-specific contribution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次制造展开：新事物被带入存在；同一种能力随后被读作性质、独创性、艺术技艺、群体资源、过程、迸发期以及特定领域的贡献。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three unrelated objects joined into one new thing that can stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：三件毫不相干的物件被拼成一个能站住的新东西。

branches.en: THE POWER AND THE PROCESS: the ability and the loop of making are both named.
branches.cn: 能力与过程：能力本身与制作循环都可用这个词指称。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: a work can be scored for newness and for difference.
branches.cn: 性质：作品可以按新颖度与差异度被打分。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: paint, sound and words give the power a body.
branches.cn: 媒介：绘画、声音与文字给这种能力一个身体。

branches.en: THE GROUP AND THE MOMENT: creativity can belong to a team or to a season.
branches.cn: 群体与时刻：创造力可以属于一个团队，也可以属于一个时期。

branches.en: THE FIELD: each discipline decides what counts as a new contribution.
branches.cn: 领域：每个学科自己决定什么算新的贡献。

intro.en: Creativity is the end of a short Latin chain: a verb of making becomes a noun, an adjective and finally an abstract noun of ability.
intro.cn: creativity 是一条简短拉丁链的末端：制造动词先成名词，再成形容词，最后成为表示能力的抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin creare gives create, creation, creator, creative and creativity; the suffixes -ive and -ity carry the chain forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 creare 衍生 create、creation、creator、creative 与 creativity；形容词与抽象名词后缀推动这条链向前。

items.meaning: the act of making or the thing made

Creativity needs both time and waste.
items.exampleCN: 创造力既需要时间，也需要浪费。
这个房间被很有创意地分隔开。

items.example: The uncreative solution copied last year's plan.
items.exampleCN: 这个缺乏创意的方案照抄了去年的计划。

items.example: The species procreates in shallow water.
items.exampleCN: 这个物种在浅水中繁殖。

definition_zh: 生物；动物；人（带怜爱或轻蔑语气）
definition_en: a living animal or person, especially one shaped by nature
core_image: 草丛里一双发亮的眼睛盯着你，看不出那是什么
scene: 夜里草丛忽然一动，一双眼睛反着月光。Something small and alive was moving in the grass, a creature we could not name.
sceneCN: 这里 creature 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：有生命的动物或人）；句意是草丛里有种小小的活物在动，一种我们叫不出名字的生物。

senses.title: A living being
senses.definition: a living animal or person
senses.definitionCN: 有生命的动物或人
senses.example: Every creature needs water and air.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个生物都需要水和空气。
senses.why: Life is what all breathing things share.
senses.whyCN: 凡是会呼吸的东西，都共享生命。

senses.title: An animal
senses.definition: an animal, especially a small or unfamiliar one
senses.definitionCN: 动物，尤指微小或不熟悉的动物
senses.example: The pond is full of tiny creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里满是微小的生物。
senses.why: A word is needed for animals too small to name.
senses.whyCN: 总得有个词来称呼小到叫不出名字的动物。

senses.title: A person, with pity
senses.definition: a person, spoken of with pity or contempt
senses.definitionCN: 带着怜悯或轻蔑去说一个人
senses.example: The poor creature had nowhere to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 这个可怜的人无处可睡。
senses.why: People are living things too, so the word can carry pity.
senses.whyCN: 人也是活物，所以这个词能带上怜悯。

intro.en: Creature comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatura, a thing made.
intro.cn: creature 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatura（被造之物）进入英语。

items.en: Creare meant to make something grow or come forth.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生长或出现。

items.en: Creatura named anything that had been brought into being.
items.cn: creatura 指一切被带进存在之中的东西。

items.en: Creature named a created living thing.
items.cn: creature 指被创造的活物。

items.en: Creature first meant any being made by God.
items.cn: creature 最初指上天所造的任何存在。

items.en: It now usually means an animal, or a person seen with pity.
items.cn: 今天它通常指动物，或带着怜悯去看的一个人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the meaning group names other living things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 这个词干，近义组列出其他表示生命体的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new
the act of making something
a person who makes something
a living thing that is not a plant
anything that is alive
a single living body

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a shape in the grass and end with a face you almost know.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从草丛里的一个影子开始，最后落到一张你几乎认得的脸。

normal.en: Create plus -ure: something created and left alive.
normal.cn: create 加 -ure：被造出来又活着的东西。

normal.en: Four legs, two eyes, one warm body.
normal.cn: 四条腿，两只眼，一具温热的身体。

normal.en: If it moves by itself, it is a creature.
normal.cn: 能自己动的东西，就是生物。

normal.en: A creature keeps no diary; it just keeps breathing.
normal.cn: 生物不写日记，它只管呼吸。

normal.en: Call it a creature when you cannot name the animal.
normal.cn: 叫不出名字时，就称它一声生物。

abstract.en: Picture eyes shining in a dark hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗树篱里发亮的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a shell moving slowly across wet sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只壳在湿沙上缓缓移动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that is not quite human.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不太像人的手。

examples.en: A small creature ran across the path.
examples.cn: 一只小生物跑过小路。

examples.en: The cave is home to creatures that avoid light.
examples.cn: 这洞穴是避光生物的家。

examples.en: She treats every creature with care.
examples.cn: 她对每个生灵都很爱护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creature 记成 create（创造）加 -ure：被造出来、还会自己动的东西，就是生物。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生长），经 creatura（被造之物）而来；本义是「被造出来的活物」，后专指动物，也可带感情地指人。

sensesIntro.en: From any living thing, to an animal, to a person spoken of with feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何活物，到动物，再到带着感情去说的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bright eyes in the grass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里草丛中两点发亮的眼睛。

branches.en: Anything alive and breathing is a creature.
branches.cn: 一切活着会呼吸的都是生物。

branches.en: Small animals are the creatures we meet most often.
branches.cn: 小动物是我们最常遇到的生物。

branches.en: A person can be called a creature when we feel pity.
branches.cn: 心里怜悯时，人可以被称为生物。

branches.en: The same word covers a beetle and a beggar.
branches.cn: 同一个词既盖住甲虫，也盖住乞丐。

branches.en: An unnamed animal is simply a creature in the dark.
branches.cn: 叫不出名的动物，就是黑暗里的一只生物。

intro.en: Creature belongs to the Latin family of creare, to make, which also gives create and creation.
intro.cn: creature 属于拉丁语 creare（制造）这一族，create 与 creation 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root creare, to bring forth, runs through the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 creare（使产生）贯穿这一整族词。

items.example: The creature slept in the leaves.
They create a new game each week.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周造一个新游戏。

items.meaning: in the manner of a creature

definition_zh: 资格证书；资历证明；凭证
definition_en: a document or record that shows a person's qualifications, training or right to be trusted
core_image: 一只打开的皮夹，里面夹着证件、推荐信与一张芯片卡
scene: 雇主在面试前先核验学历与执业记录，确认无误才安排面谈。The board verified every credential before the appointment.
sceneCN: 雇主在面试前核验学历与执业记录，确认无误才面谈；句中的 credential 指「证明资历与可信度的材料」（第 1 个义项：记录资格的文件或凭据）。图中可辨识物件：皮夹、证件、推荐信、芯片卡。

pos.zh: 资格证书；资历证明；凭证
为……提供资历证明；授予资格

senses.title: A documented qualification
senses.definition: a paper or record that proves a person's training or right to practise
senses.definitionCN: 证明某人受过训练或有执业资格的文件或记录
senses.example: The board verified every credential before the appointment.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在任命前核验了每一份资历证明。
senses.why: credere meant 'to believe, to entrust', so a credential is literally something that gives you reason to trust the bearer.
senses.whyCN: credere 意为「相信、托付」，因此 credential 字面上就是让你有理由信任持有者的东西。

senses.title: Letters of accreditation
senses.definition: the formal papers by which an envoy or a delegate is accredited
senses.definitionCN: 授予使节或代表正式身份的文书
senses.example: The ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 大使在宫中呈递了国书。
senses.why: diplomacy kept the oldest plural use: letters that vouch for a person's right to speak for a state.
senses.whyCN: 外交保留了最古老的复数用法：为某人代表国家的权利作保的信件。

senses.title: Evidence of trustworthiness
senses.definition: anything that gives others reason to rely on a person or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 任何使他人有理由依赖某人或某机构的东西
senses.example: Years of clean audits became his strongest credential.
senses.exampleCN: 多年无瑕疵的审计记录成了他最有力的信誉凭据。
senses.why: the word widened from paper to reputation: whatever makes trust reasonable can be called a credential.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从纸面扩展到声誉：凡使信任变得合理的东西都可称为凭据。

senses.title: A professional credential
senses.definition: a licence or certificate required to work in a regulated field
senses.definitionCN: 在受监管领域工作所需的执照或证书
senses.example: The hospital checks the credentials of every surgeon.
senses.exampleCN: 医院核查每位外科医生的职业资格。
senses.why: regulated work turns trust into a document, and the document is checked before a patient is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 受监管的工作把信任变成文件，并在把病人交出去之前核查这份文件。

senses.title: A digital login credential
senses.definition: the username, password or key that proves a user's identity to a system
senses.definitionCN: 向系统证明用户身份的用户名、密码或密钥
senses.example: Never store login credentials in a shared file.
senses.exampleCN: 切勿把登录凭据存放在共享文件里。
senses.why: computing extended the word to identity itself: the system must be convinced that the user is who the account says.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域把这个词扩展到身份本身：系统必须被说服，用户就是账号所称的那个人。

senses.title: Diplomatic papers
senses.definition: the documents that establish an official's status in a foreign state
senses.definitionCN: 在外国确立某官员身份的文书
senses.example: The delegation's credentials were accepted without delay.
senses.exampleCN: 代表团的国书被立即接受。
senses.why: the same plural form serves diplomacy, where a state must vouch for the person who speaks in its name.
senses.whyCN: 同一复数形式在外交中使用：国家必须为以其名义发言的人作保。

senses.title: An academic record
senses.definition: the degrees, transcripts and honours that record a student's study
senses.definitionCN: 记录一个人求学经历的学位、成绩单与荣誉
senses.example: Her academic credentials opened the door to the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学历资历为她打开了这个项目的大门。
senses.why: schools kept the oldest sense of a record that stands for a person: the transcript is the paper form of years of study.
senses.whyCN: 学校保留了最古老的「代人之记录」义：成绩单就是多年求学的纸面形态。

senses.title: To provide with credentials
senses.definition: to supply someone with the papers that establish their standing
senses.definitionCN: 为某人提供确立其身份与地位的文件
senses.example: The institute credentialed the new instructors in June.
senses.exampleCN: 研究所在六月为新讲师颁发了资质证明。
senses.why: the verb of the same spelling was formed later, and it names the authority's side of the transaction rather than the bearer's.
senses.whyCN: 同一拼写的动词形式出现较晚，命名的是权威方在这一往来中的一侧，而非持有者一侧。

intro.en: Credential comes from Medieval Latin credentialis, from Latin credentia 'belief, trust', built on credere 'to believe, to entrust'. The plural credentials named letters that accredited a envoy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: credential 来自中世纪拉丁 credentialis，源自拉丁 credentia「相信、信任」，由 credere「相信、托付」构成。复数 credentials 原指为使节授信的文书。年代为约数。

items.en: Credere meant 'to believe, to trust, to entrust'. It is the root of creed, credit and incredible, all built on the act of trusting.
items.cn: credere 意为「相信、信任、托付」，是 creed、credit 与 incredible 的词根，都建立在「信任」这一动作上。

items.en: Credentia named belief or trust, and in church use also a letter of recommendation carried by a traveller.
items.cn: credentia 指相信或信任，在教会用法中也指旅人随身携带的推荐信。

items.en: Credentialis described what gives credit or standing; the neuter plural credentialia became the set of papers carried by an envoy.
items.cn: credentialis 描述给予信用或身份之物；中性复数 credentialia 变为使节携带的一整套文书。

items.en: English took credential in the sixteenth century, first in the diplomatic plural and later as any proof of qualification.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 credential，先用于外交复数，后指任何资格证明。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to professional licensing and academic records, and in computing to the data that proves a user's identity.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词扩展到职业执照与学历记录，在计算领域则指证明用户身份的数据。

items.en: The deeper origin of credere is uncertain; the common connection to a root meaning 'to place one's heart' is a reconstruction. The exact route from church letters to professional qualifications is only partly documented.
items.cn: credere 的更早来源不确定；常被提到的、与表示「把心放上」的词根的联系属重构形式。从教会文书到职业资格的演变路径只有部分记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same believing root, each with a different job; group two holds other proofs of standing, which differ in what they guarantee.
note.cn: 第一组同出「相信」这一词根，各司不同职守；第二组是其他身份证明，所保证的内容各不相同。

entries.definition: The collected papers of standing, especially diplomatic letters; modern usage treats it as a mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指成套的身份文书，尤指国书；现代用法把它当作不可数集合名词。

entries.definition: Trust turned into financial terms: the belief that a debt will be paid.
entries.definitionCN: 信任转为金融术语：相信欠款会偿付。

entries.definition: A statement of what is believed, from the same verb but with no notion of papers.
entries.definitionCN: 指所信内容的陈述，同出该动词，却无文书之意。

entries.definition: The quality of being believable; a credential is an object that supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 指可信的性质；credential 是支撑这份性质的具体物件。

entries.definition: A single official document stating a fact; a credential may be a whole record of standing.
entries.definitionCN: 指声明某项事实的单一正式文件；credential 可以是一整套身份记录。

entries.definition: The training or exam passed, spoken of as an ability rather than a paper.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过的训练或考试，说的是能力而非纸张。

entries.definition: Legal permission to act; the credential may be the paper that carries the permission.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的法律许可；credential 可能是承载许可的纸。

entries.definition: A statement from a third party about a person, which vouches without being an official document.
entries.definitionCN: 指第三方对某人的陈述，能作保但不是正式文件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real believing root, the real diplomatic plural and the real modern digital sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的「相信」词根、真实的外交复数用法与真实的现代数字义。

normal.en: credere 'to believe': a credential gives you a reason to believe the bearer.
normal.cn: credere「相信」：credential 给你理由相信持有者。

normal.en: The plural began as diplomatic letters carried by an envoy.
normal.cn: 复数形式最初是使节携带的外交文书。

normal.en: The family runs credit, creed, credible, credibility, incredible.
normal.cn: 词族包括 credit、creed、credible、credibility、incredible。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the checks: credential verification, professional credentials, academic credentials.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出核验场景：资历核验、职业资历、学历资历。

normal.en: Computing uses it for the password that proves who you are.
normal.cn: 计算领域用它指证明「你是谁」的密码。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet whose every card is a small argument for trusting its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包，每张卡都是「请信任此人」的一小段论证。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed letter handed over at a palace gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一封密封的信在宫门处被递出。

abstract.en: Picture a system asking who you are before it will open a single door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个系统在开任何一扇门之前先问「你是谁」。

examples.en: The panel reviewed her academic credentials and two references.
examples.cn: 小组审阅了她的学历资历与两封推荐信。

examples.en: No credential substitutes for a clean safety record.
examples.cn: 任何资历证明都替代不了一份无事故的安全记录。

examples.en: The platform stores credentials in an encrypted vault.
examples.cn: 该平台把登录凭据存放在加密保险库中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cred（相信）」——让人有理由相信你的那套材料 → 资历证明、资格证书

root: 拉丁 credere「相信、托付」→ credentia「信任」→ 中世纪拉丁 credentialis／credentialia（使节文书）→ 英语 credential；credere 的更早来源不确定，与「把心放上」词根的联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one paper trail: something makes trust reasonable, and that something can be a qualification, an envoy's letters, a clean record, a licence, a password, a diplomatic document, a transcript or the act of supplying the papers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条纸面线索展开：某物使信任变得合理，而这个某物可以是资格、使节文书、清白记录、执照、密码、外交文件、成绩单，或「提供这些材料」这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wallet in which every card is a small argument for trusting the person who carries it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只钱包，每张卡都是「请信任此人」的一小段论证。

branches.en: PROOF: training records and clean audits both give reason to trust.
branches.cn: 证明：训练记录与清白审计都给出信任的理由。

branches.en: THE ENVOY: the plural began as letters that let a person speak for a state.
branches.cn: 使节：复数最初是让人代表国家发言的文书。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONS: a licence and a transcript are the same proof inside different gates.
branches.cn: 行业：执照与成绩单是不同闸门内的同一种证明。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: computing asks for proof of identity before opening a door.
branches.cn: 机器：计算领域在开门前要求身份证明。

branches.en: THE ACT: an authority supplies the papers, turning standing into something that can be shown.
branches.cn: 动作：权威方提供文件，把身份变成可出示之物。

definition_en: the quality of being believed or trusted
core_image: 记者把三份文件摊在桌上，镜头对准盖章页，编辑仍逐条核对来源
scene: 记者把三份文件摊在桌上，镜头对准盖章页，编辑仍逐条核对来源。The paper's credibility suffered after the retraction.
sceneCN: 这里指媒体被信任的程度（第 2 个义项：信誉）；句意为撤稿之后这家报纸的信誉受损。图中可辨识物件：文件、印章、镜头、核对清单。

pos.zh: 名词：可信度；可信性；信誉（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词根加表示「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可信的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「可信地」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「难以置信的」
由表示「不」的前缀加表示「相信」的词根构成，义为「不肯相信」
同一词根的名词与动词，义为「信任；信贷；把……归功于」

senses.title: Believability of a claim
senses.definition: the quality of a statement being likely to be true
senses.definitionCN: 某个说法很可能为真的性质
senses.example: The credibility of the claim depends on the source of the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法的可信度取决于数字的来源。
senses.why: Credibility is not truth itself but the likelihood that a claim is true.
senses.whyCN: 可信度不是真本身，而是一个说法为真的可能性。

senses.title: Trust in a person or institution
senses.definition: the quality of a person or body being trusted to act honestly
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构被信任会诚实行事的性质
senses.example: The newspaper's credibility fell after the retraction.
senses.exampleCN: 撤稿之后这家报纸的信誉下降。
senses.why: A reputation is built slowly and lost quickly, which is why the word often follows lose and restore.
senses.whyCN: 信誉积得慢、失得快，所以这个词常与「失去」「恢复」连用。

senses.title: Strength of research evidence
senses.definition: the quality of evidence being strong enough to be believed by experts
senses.definitionCN: 证据强到足以让专家相信的性质
senses.example: Peer review is meant to test the credibility of the findings.
senses.exampleCN: 同行评审意在检验研究结果的可信度。
senses.why: Claims that no expert can check are taken on trust alone, so the word marks the difference between belief and verification.
senses.whyCN: 无人能核验的说法只能靠信任，这个词因此标记出「相信」与「验证」之间的差别。

senses.title: The credibility gap
senses.definition: a gap between what an authority says and what people are willing to believe
senses.definitionCN: 权威所说与公众愿意相信之间的差距
senses.example: The credibility gap widened after the third denial.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次否认之后，信任差距进一步扩大。
senses.why: When official statements and visible facts diverge, trust is measured as a gap.
senses.whyCN: 当官方说法与可见事实分道扬镳，信任就被量成一道缺口。

senses.title: Media credibility
senses.definition: the trust readers place in a news organisation's reporting
senses.definitionCN: 读者对新闻机构报道的信任
senses.example: Surveys track media credibility across different outlets.
senses.exampleCN: 调查追踪不同媒体机构的公信力。
senses.why: A newsroom sells belief as much as information, so its standing is measured by this word.
senses.whyCN: 新闻机构不只卖信息，也卖相信，因此它的地位用这个词来衡量。

senses.title: Witness credibility in law
senses.definition: the quality of a witness being believed, judged by consistency and demeanour
senses.definitionCN: 证人是否被相信的性质，靠陈述一致性与举止判断
senses.example: The judge assessed the credibility of the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 法官评估了这名证人的可信性。
senses.why: Courts cannot test whether a witness is truthful directly, so they weigh consistency, motive and manner instead.
senses.whyCN: 法庭无法直接检验证人是否诚实，只能改看陈述一致性、动机与举止。

senses.title: Credibility of a threat
senses.definition: the quality of a threat being believed enough to deter action
senses.definitionCN: 威胁被相信到足以阻止行动的性质
senses.example: Deterrence rests on the credibility of the threat.
senses.exampleCN: 威慑建立在威胁的可信度上。
senses.why: A threat that no one believes changes no one's plan, so credibility is the working part of deterrence.
senses.whyCN: 无人相信的威胁改变不了任何人的计划，所以可信性才是威慑真正起作用的部分。

senses.title: Financial credibility
senses.definition: the standing of a borrower that makes lenders willing to lend
senses.definitionCN: 借款人让放贷方愿意出借的地位
senses.example: Banks reviewed the credibility of the borrower before the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在放款前审查了借款人的信用。
senses.why: Lending is a bet on future honesty, and the word names the borrower's side of that bet.
senses.whyCN: 放贷是在赌对方未来守约，这个词指借款人在这个赌局里的那一半。

senses.title: Credibility as rhetorical ethos
senses.definition: the impression of trustworthiness a speaker creates in an argument
senses.definitionCN: 演讲者在论证中造成的可信印象
senses.example: The speech gained credibility from the speaker's record of service.
senses.exampleCN: 这场演讲因演讲者长期的公共服务经历而增可信度。
senses.why: Ancient rhetoric called the speaker's apparent character ethos, and this word is its modern name.
senses.whyCN: 古代修辞学把演讲者显露的品格称作「品格诉诸」，这个词就是它的现代名称。

intro.en: Credibility comes from Latin credibilis, worthy of belief, from credere, to believe or trust. The noun credibilitas is Late Latin. English received the word through French in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 credibilis「值得相信的」，源头是动词 credere「相信、托付」。名词形式是晚期拉丁语。英语经法语在十六世纪引入。

items.en: The verb meant to believe, trust or entrust, and it also stands behind credit and creed.
items.cn: 这个动词意为相信、信任、托付，也是「信贷」与「信条」等词的源头。

items.en: The adjective meant worthy of belief, formed with the suffix of possibility.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为值得相信的，由表示可能的词尾构成。

items.en: The Late Latin noun named the quality of being believable.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语名词指「可被相信」的性质。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, first for the believability of reports.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带进英语，最初指报道的可信性。

items.en: Later usage applied it to institutions, evidence, threats and borrowers.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它用于机构、证据、威胁与借款人。

items.en: The shift from a claim being believable to a person being trusted is recorded only approximately.
items.cn: 从「说法可信」转向「人被信任」这一变化，只有大致的年代记录。

note.en: The first group shares the root or its negative; the second group names similar grounds for belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或其否定形式；第二组是类似的相信依据。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to be believed.
In a believable manner.
Not believable, or informal for astonishing.
entries.definitionCN: 指难以置信的，口语中也指惊人的。

entries.definition: Unwillingness to believe.
Trust extended to a borrower, and recognition given to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予借款人的信用，也指给予某人的肯定。

entries.definition: The quality of being easy to believe.
The quality of deserving trust.
The quality of performing consistently and dependably.
The quality of seeming reasonable rather than proven.
entries.definitionCN: 指看似合理而非已被证明。

entries.definition: A person's or body's reputation in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人或机构在某一领域的声望。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the verb to believe, and the places where belief is tested.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「相信」这个动词，以及信任受检验的各个场合。

normal.en: The root verb means to believe, so credibility is the door through which belief enters.
normal.cn: 词根意为相信，所以可信度是「相信」进入的那道门。

normal.en: A newspaper loses credibility after a retraction, which shows trust is slower to build than to lose.
normal.cn: 报纸撤稿后信誉受损，说明信任积得慢、失得快。

normal.en: Peer review is an organised test of the credibility of findings.
normal.cn: 同行评审是对研究结果可信度的制度化检验。

normal.en: Deterrence rests on the credibility of a threat, because an unbelievable threat deters no one.
normal.cn: 威慑建立在威胁的可信性上，因为无人相信的威胁吓不住人。

normal.en: Judges weigh witness credibility by consistency of account.
normal.cn: 法官靠陈述是否一致来衡量证人的可信性。

abstract.en: Credibility is a loan: others lend you their belief and watch whether you repay it.
abstract.cn: 可信度是一笔贷款：别人把信任借给你，再看你还不还。

abstract.en: Truth and trust are different currencies, and this word exchanges one for the other.
abstract.cn: 真与信任是两种货币，这个词在两者之间兑换。

abstract.en: An authority is only as strong as the gap between its words and what people see.
abstract.cn: 权威的强弱，取决于它的话与人们所见之间的那道缺口。

examples.en: The credibility of the survey was undermined by a small sample.
examples.cn: 这项调查的可信度因样本太小而受损。

examples.en: The minister never recovered the credibility lost in the scandal.
examples.cn: 部长始终未能挽回丑闻中失去的信誉。

examples.en: Cross-examination tested the credibility of each witness.
examples.cn: 交叉询问检验了每位证人的可信性。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses test belief in a claim, an institution, evidence, a gap, the media, a witness, a threat, a borrower and a speaker.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分别检验对说法、机构、证据、缺口、媒体、证人、威胁、借款人与演讲者的相信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three documents on a desk, a camera on the sealed page, and an editor still checking the source line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上三份文件、对准盖章页的镜头，以及仍在逐条核对来源的编辑。

branches.en: THE CLAIM THAT HOLDS: a statement seems likely to be true.
branches.cn: 站得住的说法：某个陈述很可能为真。

branches.en: THE TRUSTED VOICE: a person, a newsroom or a speaker earns belief.
branches.cn: 被信任的声音：个人、新闻机构或演讲者赢得相信。

branches.en: THE TESTED EVIDENCE: peer review asks whether findings deserve belief.
branches.cn: 受检验的证据：同行评审追问研究结果是否值得相信。

branches.en: THE GAP: words and visible facts drift apart, and trust is measured as a distance.
branches.cn: 缺口：言辞与可见事实分开，信任被量成距离。

branches.en: THE LEGAL, MILITARY AND FINANCIAL FORMS: a witness, a threat and a borrower must all be believed.
branches.cn: 法律、军事与财务形态：证人、威胁与借款人都必须被相信。

definition_en: trust that allows later payment, praise for something done, or a unit of study
core_image: 店主在小本子上写下你的名字，让你下个月再付钱
scene: 小店的老板没要现金，只在本子上写下他的名字。The shop gave him credit and let him pay next month.

senses.title: Buy now, pay later

senses.definitionCN: 先取货、后付款的安排
senses.example: He bought the bicycle on credit.
senses.exampleCN: 他赊账买了那辆自行车。
senses.why: Trust is written in a book and becomes money.

senses.title: Praise for what was done

senses.exampleCN: 这次救援她功不可没。
senses.why: A good act is entered under the name of the doer.
senses.whyCN: 一件好事会被记在做这件事的人名下。

senses.title: A unit of study

senses.definitionCN: 衡量一门课程完成量的单位
senses.example: The course carries four credits.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课有四个学分。
senses.why: Hours in class are counted and stored like money.
senses.whyCN: 上课的时数被数出来，像钱一样存着。

intro.cn: credit 可追到拉丁语 credere（相信）与 creditum（托付之物）。

items.en: Credere meant to believe a person or a report.
items.cn: credere 意为相信一个人或一则说法。

items.en: Creditum named money or goods entrusted to another.
items.cn: creditum 指托付给他人的钱或货物。

items.en: Credit named trust placed in a person.
items.cn: credit 指对一个人寄予的信任。

items.en: Credit came to mean trust that allows later payment.
items.cn: credit 开始指允许延后付款的信任。

items.en: Banks turned that trust into formal accounts.
items.cn: 银行把这种信任变成了正式账户。

items.en: It also means praise and a unit of study.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- stem of believing, and the meaning group names trust and borrowed money.

definition_zh: 爬行；悄悄移动；蔓延；（时间）悄然过去
definition_en: to move slowly and quietly, close to the ground or out of notice

senses.title: Move low and quiet

intro.en: Cricket comes from Old French criquet, probably from a word imitating its chirp.
intro.cn: cricket 源自法语 criquet，可能来自模仿其鸣声的词。

items.en: Criquet named the insect.
items.cn: criquet 指蟋蟀。

items.en: Cricket named the chirping insect.
items.cn: 中古英语 cricket 指鸣叫的虫。

items.en: Cricket named the bat-and-ball game.
items.cn: 十六世纪 cricket 指板球运动。

items.en: Cricket spread through English schools.
items.cn: 十八世纪板球在英国学校流行。

items.en: Not cricket named unfair conduct.
items.cn: 十九世纪 not cricket 指不光明正大。

definition_en: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
core_image: 夜里有人砸开橱窗，警报声刺破安静
scene: 玻璃碎了一地，警报在街上响起来。Stealing that car was a serious crime.
sceneCN: 这里 crime 指「罪行」（第 1 个义项：违反法律、应受惩罚的行为）；句意是偷那辆车是一项严重的罪行。

senses.title: An act against the law
senses.definition: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律、可受惩罚的行为
senses.example: Theft is a crime in every country.
senses.exampleCN: 偷窃在任何国家都是罪行。
senses.why: A rule without a penalty is only advice.
senses.whyCN: 没有惩罚的规矩，只是一句劝告。

senses.title: Illegal activity as a whole
senses.definition: illegal activity in general, seen as a social problem
senses.definitionCN: 整体而言的违法活动，被视为社会问题
senses.example: The city has cut crime by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市把犯罪减少了一半。
senses.why: Many single acts add up to one large pattern.
senses.whyCN: 许多单个行为加在一起，就成了一种大格局。

senses.title: A shameful wrong
senses.definition: something seriously wrong or shameful, though not illegal
senses.definitionCN: 严重错误或可耻的事，尽管并不违法
senses.example: It is a crime to waste such good food.
senses.exampleCN: 浪费这么好的食物简直是罪过。
senses.why: People borrow the word to weigh moral guilt.
senses.whyCN: 人们借用这个词来衡量道德上的过错。

intro.en: Crime comes from Latin crimen, a charge or accusation, through Old French.
intro.cn: crime 源自拉丁语 crimen（指控、罪名），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Crimen meant a charge or accusation.
items.cn: crimen 意为指控或罪名。

items.en: It also named the fault behind the charge.
items.cn: 它也指指控背后的那桩过错。

items.en: Crime named a wrong that could be judged.
items.cn: crime 指可受审判的过错。

items.en: Crime meant an act that broke the law.
items.cn: crime 指违反法律的行为。

items.en: It also covered illegal activity in general.
items.cn: 它也开始指整体上的违法活动。

items.en: It can even name a shameful waste.
items.cn: 它甚至可以指一种可耻的浪费。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crim- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crim- 词干，近义组列出其他表示过错与违法的说法。

normal.en: Crime begins with cry, the sound of the victim.

normal.en: A broken window is the first sentence of the story.
normal.cn: 一扇碎窗，就是这故事的第一句。

examples.en: It would be a crime to miss such a chance.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crime 记成一扇被砸碎的窗：玻璃一响，法律就记下了一桩罪行。

sensesIntro.en: From one illegal act, to illegal activity in general, to a moral wrong that no law covers.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一桩违法行为，到整体的犯罪活动，再到法律管不到的道义过错。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken shop window and a screaming alarm.

branches.en: Many such acts together become a social problem.
branches.cn: 许多这样的行为合起来，就成了社会问题。

branches.en: The word lends its weight to moral guilt.
branches.cn: 这个词把自己的分量借给了道德过错。

branches.en: The police count crimes, and the city counts crime.
